answer: Each validator locks a staking collateral C that can be released only after a zero-knowledge verifiable delay, creating a walnut of illiquid capital. The protocol applies a quadratic slashing penalty alpha*k^2 to any Sybil cluster of k identities, so marginal attack cost grows as O(k^2) while extractable reward scales linearly R*k, yielding negative expected utility. The rising tide of required capital and the accumulating dune of slashed stakes enforce a robust Nash equilibrium where rational agents prefer honest participation.
